chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “It is narrated among us in Kūfah that ʿAlī عليه السلام said: ‘Indeed, part of the completion of your hajj is your entering into ihram from the vicinity of your family’s home.’”
So he said: “Glory be to Allah! If it were as they say, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would not have remained enjoying the use of his clothes until al-Shajarah.”

key_terms.إِحْرَامُكَ: your entering into ihram, the consecrated state for pilgrimage
key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: al-Shajarah, the miqat location meant here
key_terms.بِثِيَابِهِ: in his clothes, meaning while still in ordinary dress before entering ihram
key_terms.حَجِّكَ: your hajj, referring to the pilgrimage and its proper completion
key_terms.دُوَيْرَةِ: the vicinity or immediate area, here meaning the area of one’s home
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Does a pilgrim have to enter into ihram from home, or only from the appointed miqat?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of the proper point at which ihram is assumed for hajj. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects the claim that one must enter ihram from one’s home, citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, who remained in his normal clothing until reaching the appointed miqat at al-Shajarah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2528 - It is narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "In Kufa, it is narrated that Imam Ali (as) said: 'Part of the completion of your Hajj is assuming Ihram from the vicinity of your home.'"

Imam (as) replied: "Glory be to Allah (swt)! If it were as they say, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) would not have enjoyed wearing his clothes until reaching the Tree (Dhul-Hulayfah)."
